lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.11 - A Listen, point, and say

details: Listen, point, and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows students can match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds, and confident repetition.
“I want to have a picnic but I don’t know what food to bring. Can you help me choose some food for my picnic?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.11 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle gives students controlled practice identifying the target language and differentiating between singular/plural items.
Look for accurate and confident identification and circling of the correct food item.
Amy and Nick have brought some yummy food. Can you listen and tell me what food they like?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.65 - A Look and tick

details: Look and tick strengthens recognition of target words. Students look at the pictures and locate the words that match them, reinforcing whole-word memory.
Look for correct identification of all six words, and accurate ticking of the boxes.
“I want to write down all the foods I ate at the picnic. But I’m not sure when to add s or es to the end of the words.. Can you help me?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.65 - B Look and write

details: Look and write gives students controlled practice spelling the target words and identifying individual letters within the words. It reinforces letter order and neat handwriting.
Look for correct words and spelling, consistent letter formation, and neat handwriting within the lines.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.12 - C. Trace and say

details: Trace and say gives students controlled practice of using ‘there is/there are’ to talk about food.
Look for correct use of ‘there is/there are’, and the appropriate article, and accurate identification of the objects in the picture and number of them.
“Some of the food has got separated from the rest. Can you help me match the foods?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.12 - D. Look and say

details: Look and say provides the opportunity to further use the target structure in a more engaging way.
Look for correct use of ‘there is/there are’ and the appropriate article, and natural turn-taking with classmates.
“Some other friends are also having a picnic! Can you tell me what they have?”

The chant strengthens retention of the target language and helps improve pronunciation and stress.
Look for correct stress, confident participation, with most students able to join in with at least the most repeated parts of the chant.
“That was such a fun day, with so much yummy food! Let’s say the chant together.”
